title: Pullback fit-floor never pins/clamps the camera center — the floor-clamped pullback can converge with the new district still off-screen
detail: Violates the ruled pullback contract and the PR body's own claim ("at 1.0 the full world rect is visible, so a floor-clamped target always includes the district"). Nothing pins the center. Real map 1040x780, fit=720/780 (height-bound): at zoom 1.0 visible height is exactly 780, so the full world is visible only at cy=390. A camera panned to cy=585 (valid at zoom 2.0: half_h=195, range [195,585]) that floor-clamps to 1.0 keeps cy=585 → visible y [195,975] → world y [0,195) stays cut off — the new district remains off-screen after the ~2s ease completes.
recommended_fix: In pullback_feed, run cx_to, cy_to through rnd.camera_clamp_center(..., z_to, ...) before assigning cam_wx_to/cam_wy_to (it pins the center to the world center at the fit). Add a floor test with an off-center camera asserting district inclusion.

title: pullback_feed's spawn-id derivation misattributes when a player router placement shares the frame with a growth spawn — the SEED pullback is silently skipped
detail: The feed assumes every node spawned since the last frame is a growth spawn with an event. Cmd_Place_Router also consumes a node id inside step but emits no NODE_SPAWNED; if a placement and a growth SEED land in the same inter-frame window, the derived id points at the placed router (kind != .Terminal → camera_spawn_is_seed false) and the real SEED is never classified — the ruled pullback misses its trigger.
recommended_fix: On the view side, keep the previous frame's topology.next_node_id on the App; when the event count > 0, classify EVERY node id spawned in the window (prev..next) instead of deriving ids from the event count alone.

title: Wheel-notches truncate per frame with no fractional residue — slow trackpad scrolls never fire a zoom notch
detail: PR body documents this as the old NOC-scroll precedent, but raylib accumulates only per frame — a slow two-finger trackpad scroll delivering <1.0 notch/frame truncates to factor 1.0 every frame, so zoom fires only on fast flicks. Documented minion decision, not a user ruling; minor UX edge on macOS trackpads.
recommended_fix: Keep a fractional wheel accumulator on the App (add each frame's delta, consume whole notches into camera_zoom_step, carry the residue across frames).
